statements.text: I know of several technology companies in my hometown of Huntsville that are in fact developing cyber defense technologies using AI. For instance, to address the Space and Missile Defense Command (SMDC)'s Space & Ground Systems operational cyber threat detection and prevention requirements and support the zero-trust strategy, technology is being developed to auto-configure, self-optimize, and self-train defensive models to detect and mitigate cyber threats against critical ground systems and space assets.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on AI and cyber operations in the Department of Defense.

statements.text: The generative AI use case in particular is driving the need for increased compute availability. The compute available today is insufficient to satiate demand, nor agile enough with scale to respond to what's easily knowable and foreseeable on the horizon.
statements.context: Written testimony from a DoD official responding to a congressional hearing question about AI compute and cloud infrastructure for the Department of Defense.

statements.text: Advance the system to implement Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to improve efficiency of responding. [...] Alabama A&M AI/ML are experienced in the development of algorithms from data collected to advance the protection operation from threats and make it more efficient.
statements.context: Written responses to questions from a House hearing on agroterrorism threats to the food supply chain.

statements.text: one concern is that AI allows adversaries to scale operations without scaling personnel. [...] When AI tools are misused by cyber activity what visibility, if any, does DHS and CISA have into these incidents?
statements.context: Congressional hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity, with a member questioning witnesses about DHS and CISA visibility into AI-enabled cyber threats.
